functions.name: rd_kafka_version
functions.description: Returns the librdkafka version as an integer (hex MM.mm.rr.xx). Use only for runtime checks; see RD_KAFKA_VERSION for compile-time.

functions.name: rd_kafka_version_str
functions.description: Returns the librdkafka version as a human-readable string. The returned pointer is owned by the library and must not be freed.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_get_debug_contexts
functions.description: Returns a comma-separated list of supported debug contexts at runtime for the "debug" configuration property.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_get_err_descs
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the full list of error-code descriptions and the count of entries. Intended for language bindings and diagnostics.
requirements: errdescs must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the array pointer.
cntp must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the array length.
Returned array pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify.

functions.name: rd_kafka_err2str
functions.description: Translates an rd_kafka_resp_err_t error code to a human-readable string.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_err2name
functions.description: Translates an rd_kafka_resp_err_t error code to its enum-name string (e.g., "ERR_UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID").
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned string pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_last_error
functions.description: Returns the last error code generated by a legacy API call in the current thread (e.g., consume*, produce(), etc.). Use to avoid errno conversion.
requirements: Must be called immediately after a failed legacy API call to get the correct error for the current thread.

functions.name: rd_kafka_errno2err
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Converts a system errno value to an rd_kafka_resp_err_t error code for legacy APIs. Prefer rd_kafka_last_error().
requirements: Only use for legacy APIs listed in the docs when rd_kafka_last_error() is not suitable.

functions.name: rd_kafka_errno
functions.description: DEPRECATED: Returns the thread-local errno used by librdkafka (needed on some platforms). Prefer rd_kafka_last_error().

functions.name: rd_kafka_fatal_error
functions.description: Returns the first fatal error set on the client instance (or RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR_NO_ERROR if none) and writes a human-readable error string if fatal.
requirements: rk must be a valid client instance pointer.
If a fatal error is present, errstr must point to a writable buffer of at least errstr_size bytes; only written on fatal error.

functions.name: rd_kafka_test_fatal_error
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_test_fatal_error(rd_kafka_t *rk, rd_kafka_resp_err_t err, const char *reason);
functions.description: For testing: triggers a fabricated fatal error on the client. Returns NO_ERROR if triggered, or __PREV_IN_PROGRESS if one was already triggered.
requirements: rk must be a valid client instance.
reason must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_code
functions.description: Returns the rd_kafka_resp_err_t code from an error object, or NO_ERROR if error is NULL.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_name
functions.description: Returns the error code name string (e.g., "ERR_UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID"), or empty string if error is NULL. Lifetime tied to the error object.
requirements: Do not use the returned pointer after destroying the error object.
Caller must not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable error string, or empty string if error is NULL. Lifetime tied to the error object.
requirements: Do not use the returned pointer after destroying the error object.
Caller must not free or modify the returned string.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_is_fatal
functions.description: Returns 1 if the error is fatal (client no longer usable), else 0 (also 0 if error is NULL).

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_is_retriable
functions.description: Returns 1 if the operation may be retried, else 0 (also 0 if error is NULL).

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_txn_requires_abort
functions.description: Returns 1 if the error requires aborting the current transaction (transactional API errors), else 0 (also 0 if error is NULL).
requirements: Only meaningful for errors returned by the transactional API.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_destroy
functions.description: Frees and destroys an error object. It is permitted to pass NULL as a convenience.
requirements: Do not use the error pointer after destroying it.

functions.name: rd_kafka_error_new
functions.description: Creates a new error object with the given code and optional printf-formatted message string. Mainly for mocking/testing. Must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy().
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string if provided; variadic arguments must match the format.
Returned object must be freed with rd_kafka_error_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a single rd_kafka_topic_partition_t that is not part of a list. Do not call on elements of a topic partition list.
requirements: Must not be used on elements owned by a rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t.
Do not use rktpar after destroying.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_set_leader_epoch
functions.description: Sets the partition's leader epoch (use -1 to clear). Used for fencing old leaders (KIP-320).
requirements: rktpar must be a valid partition object.
leader_epoch = -1 resets/clears the epoch.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_get_leader_epoch
functions.description: Gets the partition's leader epoch if relevant and known, else returns -1.
requirements: rktpar must be a valid partition object.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_new
functions.description: Creates a new, growable list container for topic+partitions with an initial allocation for size elements. Destroy with rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy().
requirements: Destroy the returned list with rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy
functions.description: Frees all resources used by the list and the list itself.
requirements: Do not use rkparlist after destroying it.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_add
functions.description: Adds a topic+partition to the list and returns the element so callers can fill additional fields (e.g., offset, leader epoch). Topic name is copied.
requirements: rktparlist must be a valid list created by rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_new().
topic must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_add_range
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_add_range(rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *rktparlist, const char *topic, int32_t start, int32_t stop);
functions.description: Adds a range of partitions [start..stop] for the given topic to the list.
requirements: start and stop define an inclusive range and should be valid partition IDs.
rktparlist must be valid.
topic must be a valid string.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_del
functions.description: Deletes the matching topic+partition from the list. Returns 1 if found and removed, else 0. Indices to elems[] become invalid after removal.
requirements: Do not rely on saved indices after a successful deletion (1).

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_del_by_idx
functions.description: Deletes an element by its elems[] index. Returns 1 if removed, else 0. Indices may change after removal.
requirements: idx must be within current array bounds.
Any saved indices become invalid after a successful delete.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_copy
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of a topic+partition list. Must be destroyed with rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy().
requirements: Destroy the copy with rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_set_offset
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_set_offset(rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *rktparlist, const char *topic, int32_t partition, int64_t offset);
functions.description: Sets the offset for the matching topic+partition in the list. Returns NO_ERROR or __UNKNOWN_PARTITION if not found.
requirements: topic and partition must identify an existing element in rktparlist.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_find
functions.signature: rd_kafka_topic_partition_t *rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_find(const rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *rktparlist, const char *topic, int32_t partition);
functions.description: Finds and returns the first matching element by topic+partition, or NULL if not found.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort(rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *rktparlist, int (*cmp)(const void *a, const void *b, void *cmp_opaque), void *cmp_opaque);
functions.description: Sorts the list using the provided comparator. If cmp is NULL, sorts by ascending topic name and partition. cmp_opaque is passed to the comparator.
requirements: Comparator must be consistent and must not modify list elements.
If cmp is NULL, default sort by (topic, partition) is applied.

functions.name: rd_kafka_headers_new
functions.description: Creates a new headers list preallocating space for initial_count headers. Destroy with rd_kafka_headers_destroy().
requirements: Destroy the returned headers with rd_kafka_headers_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_headers_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the headers list. Any pointers previously returned from this list become invalid.
requirements: Do not use hdrs or previously returned value pointers after destroying.

functions.name: rd_kafka_headers_copy
functions.description: Makes a deep copy of the headers list. Destroy with rd_kafka_headers_destroy().
requirements: Destroy the returned copy with rd_kafka_headers_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_add
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_header_add(rd_kafka_headers_t *hdrs, const char *name, ssize_t name_size, const void *value, ssize_t value_size);
functions.description: Adds a header entry (name,value) to the list. Name and value are copied. Supports null, empty, and proper binary values. Returns __READ_ONLY if headers are read-only, else NO_ERROR.
requirements: hdrs must be valid and not read-only for success.
If name_size is -1, name must be null-terminated; otherwise it must be at least name_size bytes.
If value_size is -1, value must be null-terminated string; otherwise value must have at least value_size bytes.

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_remove
functions.description: Removes all headers with the given key. Returns __READ_ONLY if read-only, __NOENT if no matches, else NO_ERROR.
requirements: hdrs must be valid.
name must be a valid string.

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_get_last
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_header_get_last(const rd_kafka_headers_t *hdrs, const char *name, const void **valuep, size_t *sizep);
functions.description: Finds the last header matching name. On success sets *valuep to a const pointer (possibly NULL) and *sizep to value size (trailing NUL not counted). Returns NO_ERROR if found, else __NOENT. Returned pointer is valid as long as the headers list and item live.
requirements: valuep and sizep must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs.
Do not use returned *valuep after the headers list or item is invalidated.

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_get
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_header_get(const rd_kafka_headers_t *hdrs, size_t idx, const char *name, const void **valuep, size_t *sizep);
functions.description: Iterates headers matching name using idx (start at 0, increment until NO_ERROR stops). Same semantics as rd_kafka_header_get_last for outputs.
requirements: Iterate by increasing idx starting at 0 while return is NO_ERROR.
valuep and sizep must be non-NULL.

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_get_all
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_header_get_all(const rd_kafka_headers_t *hdrs, size_t idx, const char **namep, const void **valuep, size_t *sizep);
functions.description: Iterates all headers regardless of key using idx (start at 0). On success sets pointers to key and value and value size (similar lifetime semantics).
requirements: Iterate by increasing idx starting at 0 while return is NO_ERROR.
namep, valuep, and sizep must be non-NULL.
Do not use returned pointers after hdrs is destroyed or modified.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_destroy
functions.description: Frees resources of a message and returns ownership to librdkafka. Must be called for consumed messages unless otherwise noted.
requirements: Do not use rkmessage after destroying it.
Only destroy messages you obtained from consume APIs or as documented.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_errstr
functions.description: For consumer messages: returns the error string for an errored message or NULL if no error. Must not be used for producer messages.
requirements: Only call on consumer messages; do not call on producer delivery reports.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_produce_errstr
functions.description: For producer messages: returns the error string for an errored produced message or NULL if no error. Must be used with producer.
requirements: Only call on producer delivery report messages.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_timestamp
functions.description: Returns the message timestamp in milliseconds since epoch (UTC), or -1 if not available. On output, *tstype is updated to indicate timestamp type if not NULL. Requires broker >= 0.10.0.
requirements: If tstype is non-NULL it must point to writable storage.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_latency
functions.description: Returns produce latency in microseconds from produce() call, or -1 if not available.
requirements: Only applicable for produced messages with latency tracking available.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_broker_id
functions.description: Returns the broker id the message was produced to or fetched from, or -1 if unknown.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_headers
functions.description: Gets the message headers list associated with a message. Returns NO_ERROR if headers exist, __NOENT if none, or another code if parsing failed. The returned list is associated with the message; do not use after message destruction.
requirements: hdrsp must be non-NULL to receive the headers pointer.
Do not modify or destroy the returned headers; lifetime is tied to the message unless detached.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_detach_headers
functions.description: Detaches the headers list from the message and transfers ownership to the caller (who must destroy it). The message’s headers are set to NULL. Same return semantics as rd_kafka_message_headers().
requirements: hdrsp must be non-NULL.
Caller becomes owner; must destroy with rd_kafka_headers_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_set_headers
functions.description: Replaces the message’s current headers with a new list. The message assumes ownership and will destroy the headers with the message. Existing headers, if any, are destroyed.
requirements: Do not use hdrs after passing it; ownership is transferred to the message.
Only call before the message is passed/returned to librdkafka.

functions.name: rd_kafka_header_cnt
functions.description: Returns the number of header key/value pairs in the headers list.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_status
functions.description: Returns a message’s persistence status (NOT_PERSISTED, POSSIBLY_PERSISTED, or PERSISTED). Not available in on_acknowledgement interceptors.

functions.name: rd_kafka_message_leader_epoch
functions.description: Returns the partition leader epoch when the message was fetched, if known; else -1. Only for consumed messages without error. Requires broker >= 2.10 (KIP-320).
requirements: Only call for successfully consumed messages (err == 0).

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_base64str
functions.description: Computes a base64 encoding of the given UUID. Returns a string or NULL on unsupported/failed conversion. Returned pointer lifetime is unspecified; treat as library-owned.
requirements: uuid must be a valid UUID pointer.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_least_significant_bits
functions.description: Returns the least significant 64 bits of the UUID.
requirements: uuid must be a valid UUID pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_most_significant_bits
functions.description: Returns the most significant 64 bits of the UUID.
requirements: uuid must be a valid UUID pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_new
functions.description: Creates a new UUID from the two 64-bit halves. Must be freed with rd_kafka_Uuid_destroy().
requirements: Use rd_kafka_Uuid_destroy() to free the returned UUID.

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_copy
functions.description: Creates a heap-allocated copy of the given UUID. Must be freed with rd_kafka_Uuid_destroy().
requirements: uuid must be a valid UUID pointer.
Destroy the returned UUID with rd_kafka_Uuid_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_Uuid_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a UUID created by rd_kafka_Uuid_new() or rd_kafka_Uuid_copy().
requirements: Do not use uuid after destroying it.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_new
functions.description: Create a new global configuration object with default settings. Pass the returned rd_kafka_conf_t to rd_kafka_new() (which takes ownership on success). Use rd_kafka_conf_destroy() if not used.
requirements: Must be destroyed with rd_kafka_conf_destroy() unless successfully passed to rd_kafka_new() (which assumes ownership).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a configuration object previously created with rd_kafka_conf_new(), or other conf duplication APIs. Frees all associated resources.
requirements: conf must be a valid rd_kafka_conf_t not already owned by an rd_kafka_t (i.e., not after successful rd_kafka_new()).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_dup
functions.description: Create a deep copy of an existing configuration object, except that interceptors are NOT copied.
requirements: conf must be a valid rd_kafka_conf_t.
Interceptors are not copied; if needed, re-register them on the duplicate (see interceptor notes).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_dup_filter
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_t *rd_kafka_conf_dup_filter(const rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, size_t filter_cnt, const char **filter);
functions.description: Duplicate a configuration object while filtering out properties whose names start with any of the provided prefixes.
requirements: conf must be valid.
filter must point to filter_cnt property name prefixes (strings).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf
functions.description: Return a read-only view of the configuration used by a running client instance, for extraction via rd_kafka_conf_get(), etc.
requirements: rk must be a valid rd_kafka_t.
Returned object is read-only; lifetime equals that of rk.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_conf_set(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, const char *name, const char *value, char *errstr, size_t errstr_size);
functions.description: Set a configuration property on a global conf. Topic-level properties are allowed and will be applied to the default topic configuration (creating it if necessary). On failure, writes a human-readable reason to errstr.
requirements: conf must be created by rd_kafka_conf_new().
errstr must point to a buffer of at least errstr_size bytes to receive error text on failure.
Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK, RD_KAFKA_CONF_INVALID, or RD_KAFKA_CONF_UNKNOWN.
Properties disabled at build-time return RD_KAFKA_CONF_INVALID.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_events
functions.description: Enable event sourcing for rd_kafka_event_t on queues by setting a bitmask of RD_KAFKA_EVENT_* values to be emitted for rd_kafka_queue_poll().
requirements: conf must be valid.
events is a bitmask of RD_KAFKA_EVENT_* constants.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_background_event_cb
functions.description: Register a generic event callback to be invoked from a librdkafka-managed background thread serving the background queue. Used to receive results of background-queued operations (e.g., Admin API).
requirements: event_cb must destroy the rd_kafka_event_t (rd_kafka_event_destroy()).
Must NOT call rd_kafka_destroy() from event_cb.
Conf’s opaque (set by rd_kafka_conf_set_opaque()) is passed as opaque.
Application must drop its reference to the background queue (rd_kafka_queue_destroy()) before destroying the client.
Callback is invoked from a background thread; ensure proper synchronization.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_dr_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_dr_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*dr_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, void *payload, size_t len, rd_kafka_resp_err_t err, void *opaque, void *msg_opaque));
functions.description: Deprecated. Set legacy producer delivery report callback that receives raw payload/len. Prefer rd_kafka_conf_set_dr_msg_cb() instead.
requirements: Callback runs from rd_kafka_poll() (or flush) context; application must poll regularly to receive callbacks.
Do not use for new code; prefer dr_msg_cb.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_dr_msg_cb
functions.description: Set the modern producer delivery report callback, invoked once per produced message with delivery result. Use rd_kafka_message_timestamp(), rkmessage->offset, and rkmessage->_private (msg_opaque) as needed.
requirements: Application must call rd_kafka_poll() regularly (or rd_kafka_flush()) to serve delivery reports.
With idempotent producer, retried messages may have invalid timestamp/offset (RD_KAFKA_TIMESTAMP_NOT_AVAILABLE / RD_KAFKA_OFFSET_INVALID).
Callback must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_consume_cb
functions.description: Set consumer message callback for use with rd_kafka_consumer_poll(); invoked per consumed message/event.
requirements: Callback receives conf’s opaque via rd_kafka_conf_set_opaque().
Callback must not block for long; invoked from poll context.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_rebalance_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_rebalance_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*rebalance_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, rd_kafka_resp_err_t err, rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *partitions, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set group rebalance callback for high-level consumer. Disables automatic assignment and requires the application to assign/unassign in the callback based on err (ASSIGN_PARTITIONS/REVOKE_PARTITIONS).
requirements: Must call rd_kafka_assign() for eager assignors (range/roundrobin) or rd_kafka_incremental_assign()/rd_kafka_incremental_unassign() for cooperative assignors.
On arbitrary error (neither ASSIGN_PARTITIONS nor REVOKE_PARTITIONS), call rd_kafka_assign(rk, NULL) to sync state.
The partitions list is destroyed by librdkafka on return; do not free or persist it. If modifying offsets, consider copying the list first.
Callback must be fast; it is invoked from consumer poll context.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_offset_commit_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_offset_commit_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*offset_commit_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, rd_kafka_resp_err_t err, rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *offsets, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set callback for results of automatic or manual offset commits in consumer groups. Served by rd_kafka_consumer_poll().
requirements: offsets contains per-partition committed offset and commit error.
err may be RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__NO_OFFSET when there was nothing to commit (not an error).
Callback must be fast; called from poll context.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_error_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_error_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*error_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, int err, const char *reason, void *opaque));
functions.description: Register error callback to receive warnings and errors. Most are informational and transient; use rd_kafka_fatal_error() if err == RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__FATAL to retrieve fatal error details and begin termination.
requirements: If no error_cb is set (or RD_KAFKA_EVENT_ERROR not enabled), errors are logged instead.
Callback is invoked from internal threads or poll context; it must not block.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_throttle_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_throttle_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*throttle_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, const char *broker_name, int32_t broker_id, int throttle_time_ms, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set throttle callback to receive broker throttle times for Produce/Fetch. Requires broker >= 0.9.0.
requirements: Application must poll regularly to serve callbacks.
Callback must be fast; invoked from poll context.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_log_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_log_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, void (*log_cb)(const rd_kafka_t *rk, int level, const char *fac, const char *buf));
functions.description: Set application log sink callback (alternative to stderr or syslog). Use with log.queue to forward logs to a queue. Do not perform prolonged work in callback unless logs are forwarded to a queue.
requirements: If logs are not forwarded (via rd_kafka_set_log_queue and log.queue=true), callback may be called from internal threads; must not call librdkafka APIs or block.
Pass NULL to disable logging.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_stats_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_stats_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*stats_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, char *json, size_t json_len, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set statistics callback, invoked from rd_kafka_poll() every statistics.interval.ms. Receives a JSON string; return 1 to take ownership (free later), or 0 to let librdkafka free immediately.
requirements: Enable statistics via statistics.interval.ms > 0.
Callback must be fast; invoked from poll context.
If returning 1, the application must later free the json pointer.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_oauthbearer_token_refresh_cb
functions.description: Set SASL/OAUTHBEARER token refresh callback. Triggered via poll() or SASL queue when a token is needed. Callback should call rd_kafka_oauthbearer_set_token() or rd_kafka_oauthbearer_set_token_failure().
requirements: For initial connection, application must either poll to trigger refresh or enable SASL queue/background callbacks (rd_kafka_conf_enable_sasl_queue + forwarding / rd_kafka_sasl_background_callbacks_enable).
Mutually exclusive with enable.sasl.oauthbearer.unsecure.jwt=true.
Callback must be fast and non-blocking.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_enable_sasl_queue
functions.description: Enable/disable a dedicated SASL event queue for SASL callbacks (currently OAUTHBEARER). Retrieve with rd_kafka_queue_get_sasl().
requirements: Call prior to creating the client.
When enabled, application must serve or forward the SASL queue (e.g., to background queue).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_socket_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_socket_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*socket_cb)(int domain, int type, int protocol, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set custom socket creation callback. Should create sockets with CLOEXEC race-free if possible.
requirements: Callback will be called from internal threads; must be thread-safe and non-blocking beyond OS call.
Must return a valid fd or -1 with errno set.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_connect_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_connect_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*connect_cb)(int sockfd, const struct sockaddr *addr, int addrlen, const char *id, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set custom connect callback, responsible for connecting sockfd to addr. Return 0 on success or errno value on error.
requirements: Called from internal threads; must be thread-safe.
sockfd is created by socket_cb (or default).
Return 0 on success, or a POSIX errno value on error.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_closesocket_cb
functions.description: Set custom close-socket callback for sockets opened by the client.
requirements: Called from internal threads; must be thread-safe.
Return value is ignored (implementation-defined).

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_open_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_open_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*open_cb)(const char *pathname, int flags, mode_t mode, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set custom open() callback (non-Windows) for opening files with CLOEXEC race-free if possible.
requirements: Only available on non-Windows platforms.
Called from internal threads; must be thread-safe.
Must return a valid fd or -1 with errno set.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_resolve_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_conf_set_resolve_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*resolve_cb)(const char *node, const char *service, const struct addrinfo *hints, struct addrinfo **res, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set address resolution callback (getaddrinfo-like). Also called with all NULL parameters to free addrinfo stored in res (must succeed).
requirements: Callback called from internal threads; must be thread-safe.
When called with node=NULL,service=NULL,hints=NULL, must free *res and return success (return value ignored).
Otherwise return getaddrinfo-style code and set *res.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_cert_verify_cb
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_cert_verify_cb(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, int (*ssl_cert_verify_cb)(rd_kafka_t *rk, const char *broker_name, int32_t broker_id, int *x509_error, int depth, const char *buf, size_t size, char *errstr, size_t errstr_size, void *opaque));
functions.description: Set SSL broker certificate verification callback. Called for each certificate in the chain upon connecting. Return 1 (valid) or 0 (invalid) and optionally set x509_error and write errstr on failure.
requirements: Called from internal threads; must be thread-safe and non-blocking.
errstr must be written (<= errstr_size including NUL) when returning 0.
Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK if SSL supported; RD_KAFKA_CONF_INVALID otherwise.
May set *x509_error to non-zero to set SSL context error. If returning 1 and setting x509_error to 0 while original was non-zero, clears SSL error.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_cert
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_conf_set_ssl_cert(rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, rd_kafka_cert_type_t cert_type, rd_kafka_cert_enc_t cert_enc, const void *buffer, size_t size, char *errstr, size_t errstr_size);
functions.description: Load a certificate/key/CA into the configuration from an in-memory buffer with the given encoding (PKCS12/DER/PEM).
requirements: Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK on success; RD_KAFKA_CONF_INVALID if encoding invalid or SSL not supported.
Passing buffer=NULL clears the configuration for cert_type.
Private key may require ssl.key.password to be set before calling.
OpenSSL 3.0 with obsolete cipher may require legacy provider via OPENSSL_CONF.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_engine_callback_data
functions.description: Set OpenSSL engine callback_data (e.g., used by ENGINE_load_ssl_client_cert). Requires ssl.engine.location configured.
requirements: callback_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the configuration and any clients created from it.
ssl.engine.location must be set for this to have effect.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_opaque
functions.description: Set an application-defined opaque pointer to be passed to callbacks registered on this conf.
requirements: opaque must remain valid as long as callbacks may reference it (typically until client is destroyed).

functions.name: rd_kafka_opaque
functions.description: Retrieve the opaque pointer previously set with rd_kafka_conf_set_opaque() for this client instance.
requirements: rk must be valid.
Returns the pointer set during configuration.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_set_default_topic_conf
functions.description: Deprecated. Set the default topic configuration for automatically subscribed topics. Replaces any implicit default topic conf on the global conf. The tconf becomes owned by conf.
requirements: Do not use tconf after this call; its lifetime is tied to conf.
Overwrites any default topic-level properties already set on the global conf.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_get_default_topic_conf
functions.description: Get the default topic configuration currently associated with a global conf, if any. The object is owned by conf; may be modified but not destroyed.
requirements: Returned pointer must not be destroyed; lifetime is tied to conf or until next rd_kafka_conf_set_default_topic_conf().

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_get
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_conf_get(const rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, const char *name, char *dest, size_t *dest_size);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of a configuration property by name into dest. If dest is NULL, only the full length is returned via dest_size. Topic-level properties may be retrieved via the default_topic_conf fallback.
requirements: dest_size must point to a size_t that will be updated with the full length (regardless of dest).
If dest is non-NULL, ensure it has at least *dest_size bytes or call twice to size then fetch.
Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK if property name matched; RD_KAFKA_CONF_UNKNOWN otherwise.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_get
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_topic_conf_get(const rd_kafka_topic_conf_t *conf, const char *name, char *dest, size_t *dest_size);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of a topic configuration property. Same semantics as rd_kafka_conf_get().
requirements: dest_size must be provided and will be updated with full length.
Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK on success or RD_KAFKA_CONF_UNKNOWN if name not recognized.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_dump
functions.description: Dump all configuration property names and values of a global conf to a newly allocated array of alternating "key","value" strings. Free with rd_kafka_conf_dump_free().
requirements: cntp will be set to the number of strings in the array (pairs of key,value).
Caller must free with rd_kafka_conf_dump_free(arr, cnt).

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_dump
functions.description: Dump all topic configuration properties for a topic conf to an array of alternating "key","value" strings. Free with rd_kafka_conf_dump_free().
requirements: cntp will be set to number of strings.
Must free with rd_kafka_conf_dump_free().

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_dump_free
functions.description: Free a configuration dump previously returned by rd_kafka_conf_dump() or rd_kafka_topic_conf_dump().
requirements: Pass the same cnt as returned by dump.
arr must be the pointer returned by dump.

functions.name: rd_kafka_conf_properties_show
functions.description: Print a table of all supported configuration properties, their defaults, and descriptions to the given FILE*. Shows all properties even if disabled at build time.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* for writing.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_new
functions.description: Create a new topic configuration object with defaults.
requirements: Destroy with rd_kafka_topic_conf_destroy() unless passed to rd_kafka_topic_new() (which takes ownership on success).

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_dup
functions.description: Create a duplicate of an existing topic configuration object.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_default_topic_conf_dup
functions.description: Create a duplicate of a client instance’s default topic configuration.
requirements: rk must be a valid rd_kafka_t.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a topic configuration object.
requirements: topic_conf must not be owned by a conf/client (i.e., not after successful rd_kafka_topic_new() that took ownership).

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_set
functions.signature: rd_kafka_conf_res_t rd_kafka_topic_conf_set(rd_kafka_topic_conf_t *conf, const char *name, const char *value, char *errstr, size_t errstr_size);
functions.description: Set a topic-level configuration property.
requirements: errstr buffer should be provided to receive error text on failure.
Returns RD_KAFKA_CONF_OK, RD_KAFKA_CONF_INVALID, or RD_KAFKA_CONF_UNKNOWN.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_set_opaque
functions.description: Set topic-level opaque pointer passed to topic callbacks as rkt_opaque.
requirements: rkt_opaque must remain valid while used by callbacks.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_set_partitioner_cb
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_topic_conf_set_partitioner_cb(rd_kafka_topic_conf_t *topic_conf, int32_t (*partitioner)(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *keydata, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque));
functions.description: Set custom producer partitioner callback for the topic.
requirements: Partitioner must NOT call any rd_kafka_*() except rd_kafka_topic_partition_available().
Partitioner must be fast and non-blocking; may be called multiple times per message.
Must return 0..partition_cnt-1, or RD_KAFKA_PARTITION_UA to indicate failure.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_conf_set_msg_order_cmp
functions.description: Experimental. Set custom comparator for per-topic message queue insertion ordering (affects retry ordering, not FIFO when queuing.strategy=fifo).
requirements: Comparator must be stable and must NOT call any rd_kafka_*() functions.
Must be fast and non-blocking.
Experimental API: subject to change/removal.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_partition_available
functions.description: Check if a partition currently has an active leader broker (producer partitioner helper).
requirements: Must only be called from inside a partitioner callback.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_random
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_random(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in random partitioner. Avoids unavailable partitions.
requirements: For producer use via partitioner_cb or as default. Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_consistent
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_consistent(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in consistent (CRC-based) partitioner mapping identical keys to identical partitions.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1 based on key.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_consistent_random
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_consistent_random(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in consistent-random partitioner: keyed messages use consistent hash; keyless go to random partition.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_murmur2
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_murmur2(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in Murmur2 (Java-compatible) consistent partitioner for keyed messages.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_murmur2_random
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_murmur2_random(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in Murmur2 consistent-random partitioner: keys use Murmur2 hashing; keyless use random.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_fnv1a
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_fnv1a(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in FNV-1a consistent partitioner for keyed messages.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_fnv1a_random
functions.signature: int32_t rd_kafka_msg_partitioner_fnv1a_random(const rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, const void *key, size_t keylen, int32_t partition_cnt, void *rkt_opaque, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Built-in FNV-1a consistent-random partitioner: keys use FNV-1a hashing; keyless use random.
requirements: Returns 0..partition_cnt-1.

functions.name: rd_kafka_new
functions.signature: rd_kafka_t *rd_kafka_new(rd_kafka_type_t type, rd_kafka_conf_t *conf, char *errstr, size_t errstr_size);
functions.description: Create a new Kafka client instance (producer or consumer). On success, the conf is owned by the client; on failure, returns NULL and writes error text to errstr.
requirements: type must be RD_KAFKA_PRODUCER or RD_KAFKA_CONSUMER.
conf may be NULL or a conf created by rd_kafka_conf_new(); on success do not destroy conf.
errstr must point to a buffer of at least errstr_size for error text on failure.
For consumers, do not mix legacy simple consumer APIs with high-level consumer APIs on the same handle.

functions.name: rd_kafka_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a Kafka client handle. Blocks until internal termination completes. For consumers with group.id, will implicitly call rd_kafka_consumer_close() unless disabled via rd_kafka_destroy_flags().
requirements: May trigger consumer callbacks (e.g., rebalance_cb) unless RD_KAFKA_DESTROY_F_NO_CONSUMER_CLOSE is used via rd_kafka_destroy_flags().

functions.name: rd_kafka_destroy_flags
functions.description: Destroy a Kafka handle with control flags. Use RD_KAFKA_DESTROY_F_NO_CONSUMER_CLOSE to avoid implicit consumer_close and consumer callbacks.
requirements: flags is a bitmask; currently RD_KAFKA_DESTROY_F_NO_CONSUMER_CLOSE=0x8.

functions.name: rd_kafka_name
functions.description: Return the client instance name.
requirements: rk must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_type
functions.description: Return the handle type (RD_KAFKA_PRODUCER or RD_KAFKA_CONSUMER).
requirements: rk must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_memberid
functions.description: Return the broker-assigned group member id as an allocated string (requires high-level consumer).
requirements: Caller must free the returned string with free() or rd_kafka_mem_free().
May return NULL if not available.

functions.name: rd_kafka_clusterid
functions.description: Return the ClusterId string (allocated) from metadata, waiting up to timeout_ms if not cached. Requires broker >=0.10.0 and api.version.request=true.
requirements: Caller must free returned string with rd_kafka_mem_free().
May return NULL if not retrievable within timeout.

functions.name: rd_kafka_controllerid
functions.description: Return the current controller broker id, or -1 if unavailable within timeout. Requires broker >=0.10.0 and api.version.request=true.
requirements: rk must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_new
functions.description: Create a new topic handle (refcounted). Returns existing handle if same name already created. On success, takes ownership of conf. Destroy with rd_kafka_topic_destroy().
requirements: On error returns NULL; convert errno with rd_kafka_errno2err().
Must eventually call rd_kafka_topic_destroy() per successful creation.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_destroy
functions.description: Decrease app reference count to a topic handle created with rd_kafka_topic_new().
requirements: Object may not be destroyed immediately if held internally; app must treat as destroyed.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_name
functions.description: Return the topic name.
requirements: rkt must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_topic_opaque
functions.description: Return the topic-level opaque pointer set via rd_kafka_topic_conf_set_opaque().
requirements: rkt must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_poll
functions.description: Poll the client for events, serving callbacks (delivery reports, error_cb, stats_cb, throttle_cb, oauthbearer token refresh). Blocks up to timeout_ms ms (-1 forever, 0 non-blocking).
requirements: Applications should call poll() regularly to serve callbacks unless using background/event queues.
If using dr_msg_cb or error_cb, polling is generally required.

functions.name: rd_kafka_yield
functions.description: Cancel the current callback dispatcher (e.g., from inside a callback) to return early to the poller.
requirements: Must ONLY be called from within a librdkafka callback.

functions.name: rd_kafka_pause_partitions
functions.description: Pause producing or consumption for specified partitions. Per-partition status in .err of the list.
requirements: partitions must list topic/partition pairs to pause.

functions.name: rd_kafka_resume_partitions
functions.description: Resume producing/consumption for specified partitions. Per-partition status in .err.
requirements: partitions must list topic/partition pairs to resume.

functions.name: rd_kafka_query_watermark_offsets
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_query_watermark_offsets(rd_kafka_t *rk, const char *topic, int32_t partition, int64_t *low, int64_t *high, int timeout_ms);
functions.description: Query broker for beginning (low) and end (high) offsets for a topic-partition, waiting up to timeout_ms.
requirements: topic/partition must exist.
low and high must be valid pointers.

functions.name: rd_kafka_get_watermark_offsets
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_get_watermark_offsets(rd_kafka_t *rk, const char *topic, int32_t partition, int64_t *low, int64_t *high);
functions.description: Get last known cached low/high offsets for a topic-partition. For consumers only; high is updated on each fetch, low periodically.
requirements: If no cached values, returns RD_KAFKA_OFFSET_INVALID via pointers.
Use with active consumer instance.

functions.name: rd_kafka_offsets_for_times
functions.description: For each topic-partition in offsets, with .offset set to a timestamp (ms since epoch), find the earliest offset with timestamp >= given timestamp. Updates .offset on output. Per-partition errors in .err.
requirements: offsets must not be empty; duplicate topic+partitions not supported.
Returns NO_ERROR if query attempted; per-partition .err may indicate failures.
May return TIMED_OUT if not all fetched; INVALID_ARG if empty list.

functions.name: rd_kafka_mem_calloc
functions.description: Allocate zeroed memory using librdkafka’s allocator (typically calloc). Use rd_kafka_mem_free() to free.
requirements: If memory is intended for APIs that require matching free, free with rd_kafka_mem_free().

functions.name: rd_kafka_mem_malloc
functions.description: Allocate memory using librdkafka’s allocator (typically malloc). Use rd_kafka_mem_free() to free.
requirements: Free with rd_kafka_mem_free() for pointers returned by APIs that document this requirement.

functions.name: rd_kafka_mem_free
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated by librdkafka APIs that require rd_kafka_mem_free().
requirements: Only use for pointers explicitly documented to be freed by this function.
If memory came from an API tied to a specific rk, pass that rk; else pass NULL.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_new
functions.description: Create a new (initially empty) event/message queue.
requirements: Destroy with rd_kafka_queue_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a queue, purging all enqueued elements and releasing references.
requirements: If destroying consumer queue (from rd_kafka_queue_get_consumer), must destroy it before rd_kafka_consumer_close().

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_get_main
functions.description: Get a reference to the main event queue (served by rd_kafka_poll()).
requirements: Release reference with rd_kafka_queue_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_get_sasl
functions.description: Get a reference to the SASL callback queue if a SASL mechanism with callbacks is configured (currently OAUTHBEARER), else NULL.
requirements: Release with rd_kafka_queue_destroy().
Enable with rd_kafka_conf_enable_sasl_queue() before client creation.

functions.name: rd_kafka_sasl_background_callbacks_enable
functions.description: Enable serving SASL OAUTHBEARER refresh callbacks on the background thread (alternative to polling).
requirements: Returns NULL on success or error object on failure (destroy with rd_kafka_error_destroy()).

functions.name: rd_kafka_sasl_set_credentials
functions.description: Set or update SASL PLAIN/SCRAM username/password credentials for this client. New credentials are used for subsequent authentications.
requirements: Applies only to SASL PLAIN and SCRAM mechanisms.
Does not disconnect existing authenticated connections.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_get_consumer
functions.description: Get a reference to the consumer queue (served by rd_kafka_consumer_poll()). Polling this queue counts as consumer poll for max.poll.interval.ms tracking.
requirements: Must destroy this queue via rd_kafka_queue_destroy() prior to rd_kafka_consumer_close().
If forwarded, polling destination queue also counts as consumer poll.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_get_partition
functions.description: Get a reference to a partition’s fetch queue (consumers only), or NULL if invalid partition.
requirements: Must destroy with rd_kafka_queue_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_get_background
functions.description: Get a reference to the background thread queue, or NULL if background queue is not enabled. This queue is polled by librdkafka and must NOT be polled/forwarded by the app; only pass as dest queue to APIs.
requirements: Release reference with rd_kafka_queue_destroy().
Do not poll or forward this queue; librdkafka owns it.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_forward
functions.description: Forward/re-route all events from src queue to dst queue. Pass dst=NULL to remove forwarding. Adjusts internal references.
requirements: After calling, src will not forward its fetch queue to the consumer queue regardless of dst.

functions.name: rd_kafka_set_log_queue
functions.description: Forward librdkafka logs to the specified queue (or main queue if rkqu==NULL) to be served by a poll call. Requires log.queue=true.
requirements: Returns _NO_ERROR on success, _NOT_CONFIGURED if log.queue is not true.
librdkafka keeps its own reference to the provided queue.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_length
functions.description: Return the current number of elements in a queue.
requirements: rkqu must be valid.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_io_event_enable
functions.signature: void rd_kafka_queue_io_event_enable(rd_kafka_queue_t *rkqu, int fd, const void *payload, size_t size);
functions.description: Enable IO event triggering for a queue: librdkafka writes payload to fd when a previously empty queue receives a new element. Set fd=-1 to disable.
requirements: fd/socket must be non-blocking.
IO and callback event triggering are mutually exclusive.
For forwarded queues, enable IO only on the final destination queue.
librdkafka keeps a copy of payload.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_cb_event_enable
functions.description: Enable callback event triggering for a queue: event_cb is called from internal thread when a previously empty queue gets a new element. Pass event_cb=NULL to disable.
requirements: IO and callback triggering are mutually exclusive.
Callback must not perform prolonged work or call librdkafka APIs for the same rd_kafka_t.

functions.name: rd_kafka_queue_yield
functions.description: Cancel the current rd_kafka_queue_poll() to return immediately. Can be called from another thread (not signal-safe).
requirements: Must not be called from signal handlers (may deadlock).

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_start
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_consume_start(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int64_t offset);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: start consuming from topic-partition at offset (absolute or logical: BEGINNING/END/STORED/TAIL).
requirements: Must not be called multiple times for same topic/partition without rd_kafka_consume_stop().
Returns 0 on success or -1 on error, with errno set (convert with rd_kafka_errno2err()).
Requires proper group.id for STORED offset mode.
offset may be RD_KAFKA_OFFSET_BEGINNING/END/STORED or RD_KAFKA_OFFSET_TAIL(CNT).

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_start_queue
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_consume_start_queue(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int64_t offset, rd_kafka_queue_t *rkqu);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: start consuming and re-route fetched messages to the provided queue. Must not be mixed with consume_start() for same topic/partition.
requirements: rkqu must be created with rd_kafka_queue_new().
Requires rd_kafka_consume_stop() before restarting.
Use rd_kafka_consume_*_queue() functions to consume.

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_stop
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: stop consuming for topic/partition and purge local queue. Blocks until fetcher stops and offsets are committed to configured store.
requirements: Returns 0 on success or -1 on error (errno).
All consumers must be stopped before destroying the main handle.

functions.name: rd_kafka_seek
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_seek(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int64_t offset, int timeout_ms);
functions.description: Deprecated: Seek the consumer’s fetch position for a topic/partition to an absolute or logical offset. Optionally wait up to timeout_ms for state update. Purges pre-fetched messages.
requirements: Partition must be already assigned/consumed; use rd_kafka_assign() to set initial offsets.
If timeout_ms==0, operation is initiated asynchronously.
May return _TIMED_OUT if not updated in time.

functions.name: rd_kafka_seek_partitions
functions.description: Seek the consumer fetch position for multiple partitions to per-partition offsets (absolute or logical). Optionally wait up to timeout_ms. Purges pre-fetched data. Per-partition errors in .err.
requirements: Partitions must be currently assigned/consumed; use assign APIs for initial offsets.
Returns NULL on success; otherwise an error object (destroy when done).

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: consume one message/event from topic/partition, waiting up to timeout_ms ms. Returns rd_kafka_message_t* which must be destroyed with rd_kafka_message_destroy().
requirements: rd_kafka_consume_start() must have been called previously.
On error returns NULL; errno set (ETIMEDOUT, ENOENT).
Check rkmessage->err for PARTITION_EOF (not an error) and others.

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_batch
functions.signature: ssize_t rd_kafka_consume_batch(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int timeout_ms, rd_kafka_message_t **rkmessages, size_t rkmessages_size);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: consume up to rkmessages_size messages into provided array for topic/partition. Higher throughput than rd_kafka_consume().
requirements: rd_kafka_consume_start() must have been called.
Returns number of messages (0 on timeout) or -1 on error.
Each returned message must be destroyed with rd_kafka_message_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_callback
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_consume_callback(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int timeout_ms, void (*consume_cb)(rd_kafka_message_t *rkmessage, void *commit_opaque), void *commit_opaque);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: consume and invoke callback per message for topic/partition. Higher throughput; deprecated API.
requirements: Callback must not destroy the message; librdkafka owns it.
Returns number of messages processed or -1 on error.
Deprecated; prefer poll/queue-based alternatives.

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_queue
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: consume a message from a queue obtained via consume_start_queue().
requirements: Return must be destroyed with rd_kafka_message_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_batch_queue
functions.signature: ssize_t rd_kafka_consume_batch_queue(rd_kafka_queue_t *rkqu, int timeout_ms, rd_kafka_message_t **rkmessages, size_t rkmessages_size);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: batch consume from a queue.
requirements: Returns count (0 on timeout) or -1 on error; destroy each message.

functions.name: rd_kafka_consume_callback_queue
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_consume_callback_queue(rd_kafka_queue_t *rkqu, int timeout_ms, void (*consume_cb)(rd_kafka_message_t *rkmessage, void *commit_opaque), void *commit_opaque);
functions.description: Legacy simple consumer: callback-based consume from a queue. Deprecated.
requirements: Callback must not destroy message.
Returns number processed or -1 on error.

functions.name: rd_kafka_offset_store
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_offset_store(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int64_t offset);
functions.description: Deprecated; store offset+1 for topic/partition for next auto-commit/manual offset-less commit.
requirements: Partition must be currently assigned (else _STATE).
Avoid storing after seek; store prior to seek.
enable.auto.offset.store must be false when using this API.
Returns NO_ERROR or error.

functions.name: rd_kafka_offsets_store
functions.description: Store offsets (as-is; not +1) for multiple partitions for next auto-commit/manual offset-less commit. Uses leader epoch if set.
requirements: Partitions must be currently assigned; non-assigned fail with _STATE.
Avoid storing after seek; store prior.
enable.auto.offset.store must be false.
Returns NO_ERROR on (partial) success; INVALID_ARG if auto offset store is true; UNKNOWN_PARTITION/STATE if none could be stored.

functions.name: rd_kafka_offset_store_message
functions.description: Store message’s offset+1 for the consumed message for next auto/manual commit.
requirements: Partition must be currently assigned; else returns error (_STATE).
Avoid storing after seek; store prior.
enable.auto.offset.store must be false.
Returns NULL on success or error object to be destroyed.

functions.name: rd_kafka_subscribe
functions.description: High-level consumer: subscribe to a set of topics (supports regex by leading '^'). Asynchronous; rejoin group, rebalance, assign, then start fetching.
requirements: Only .topic field of list is used; others ignored.
Unreachable topics result in consumer errors on poll (UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PART or TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED), not as subscribe() return.
Returns NO_ERROR, INVALID_ARG on invalid/empty list, or _FATAL if a fatal error was raised.

functions.name: rd_kafka_unsubscribe
functions.description: High-level consumer: unsubscribe from current subscription set.

functions.name: rd_kafka_subscription
functions.description: High-level consumer: get current subscription list (possibly empty). Allocates a new list which the caller must destroy.
requirements: Caller must destroy the returned list with rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy().

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_poll
functions.description: Poll the high-level consumer for a single message or event. Blocks up to timeout_ms milliseconds. Returns a message when err==RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR_NO_ERROR, or an event/error otherwise. Must be called regularly to serve queued callbacks (rebalance, error, stats, etc.). Using subscriptions requires polling at least every max.poll.interval.ms to remain in the group.
requirements: rk must be a consumer handle created with rd_kafka_new(RD_KAFKA_CONSUMER, ..)
timeout_ms >= -1 (use 0 for non-blocking, -1 to wait indefinitely)
Caller must check returned rd_kafka_message_t->err to distinguish message vs. event error
Caller must destroy returned message with rd_kafka_message_destroy() when done
on_consume() interceptors may be invoked before delivery

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_close
functions.description: Close the high-level consumer, revoking assignment, optionally committing offsets, and leaving the consumer group. Blocks roughly up to session.timeout.ms. After return, destroy the handle with rd_kafka_destroy().
requirements: rk must be a consumer instance
Application must continue to call rd_kafka_destroy() after successful close
Callbacks (e.g., rebalance_cb) may be invoked during close; ensure thread-safety

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_close_queue
functions.description: Asynchronously close the consumer. Performs the same actions as rd_kafka_consumer_close() but in a background thread. Rebalance and other events will be forwarded to rkqu, which the application must poll until rd_kafka_consumer_closed() returns true.
requirements: rk must be a consumer instance
rkqu must be a valid queue; application must poll rkqu until rd_kafka_consumer_closed(rk) returns 1
Returned error object must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_closed
functions.description: Return 1 if the consumer is fully closed after an asynchronous close (rd_kafka_consumer_close_queue()), else 0.
requirements: Call after initiating rd_kafka_consumer_close_queue()
rk must be the same consumer instance

functions.name: rd_kafka_incremental_assign
functions.description: Incrementally add partitions to the current assignment for cooperative assignors during rebalance (err==ASSIGN_PARTITIONS). May also be used outside the rebalance callback.
requirements: For cooperative assignors, pass the partitions provided by the rebalance callback (or a copy), even if empty
partitions must not be NULL
Returned error must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL

functions.name: rd_kafka_incremental_unassign
functions.description: Incrementally remove partitions from the current assignment for cooperative assignors during rebalance (err==REVOKE_PARTITIONS). May also be used outside the rebalance callback.
requirements: For cooperative assignors, pass the partitions provided by the rebalance callback (or a copy), even if empty
partitions must not be NULL
Returned error must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL

functions.name: rd_kafka_rebalance_protocol
functions.description: Return the rebalance protocol currently in use: "NONE" (not joined), "EAGER", or "COOPERATIVE".
requirements: rk must be a consumer instance
Return value is a pointer valid for the lifetime of rk; do not free

functions.name: rd_kafka_assign
functions.description: Atomically set the consumer’s assignment. Replaces existing assignment. Passing a zero-length list sets an empty assignment while preserving join state; passing NULL clears internal state.
requirements: Use the rebalance callback’s provided list (or a copy) during rebalance
Use empty (not NULL) list in rebalance callback to maintain join state
Check return value for RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__FATAL indicating a fatal error

functions.name: rd_kafka_assignment
functions.description: Retrieve the current assignment as set by assign()/incremental_assign(). Allocates a list into *partitions; caller must destroy it.
requirements: rk must be a consumer instance
Caller must free *partitions using rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_destroy() on success

functions.name: rd_kafka_assignment_lost
functions.description: Return 1 if the current assignment is considered lost (typically only useful during a rebalance event), else 0. Calling assign()/incremental_* resets this flag.
requirements: Use from rebalance event handling or shortly thereafter
rk must be a consumer instance

functions.name: rd_kafka_commit
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_commit(rd_kafka_t *rk, const rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *offsets, int async);
functions.description: Commit offsets on broker for specified partitions, or the current assignment if offsets is NULL. If async==0, blocks until commit completes; if async!=0, schedules commit and returns.
requirements: If offsets is provided, .offset should be last processed + 1
Caller must poll to receive commit callback if configured
Check for RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__FATAL to detect fatal consumer error

functions.name: rd_kafka_commit_message
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_commit_message(rd_kafka_t *rk, const rd_kafka_message_t *rkmessage, int async);
functions.description: Commit the offset of a single message (message->offset + 1) for its partition. Supports async or sync behavior like rd_kafka_commit().
requirements: rkmessage must be from this consumer instance
If async==0, may block until commit completes

functions.name: rd_kafka_commit_queue
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_commit_queue(rd_kafka_t *rk, const rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *offsets, rd_kafka_queue_t *rkqu, void (*cb)(rd_kafka_t *, rd_kafka_resp_err_t, rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_t *, void *), void *commit_opaque);
functions.description: Commit offsets and post the result to a specified queue. If rkqu is NULL a temporary queue is used and cb is served in this call. If rkqu is non-NULL, poll that queue to receive the result (and cb will be invoked if provided).
requirements: If rkqu is NULL, cb will be invoked synchronously in this call
If rkqu is non-NULL and cb==NULL, application must poll rkqu to receive the RD_KAFKA_EVENT_COMMIT event and may read opaque with rd_kafka_event_opaque()
offsets may be NULL to commit current assignment

functions.name: rd_kafka_committed
functions.description: Retrieve committed offsets for the given topic-partitions; populates each element’s .offset or .err. Respects isolation.level (read_committed vs read_uncommitted).
requirements: partitions must specify topic and partition
timeout_ms >= 0
Per-partition results returned in list elements; caller must check .err

functions.name: rd_kafka_position
functions.description: Retrieve current positions (last consumed offset + 1) for specified partitions, or RD_KAFKA_OFFSET_INVALID if none.
requirements: Consumer must be active and assigned these partitions
Caller must check per-element .err

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata
functions.description: Return the current consumer group metadata for passing to the transactional producer’s rd_kafka_send_offsets_to_transaction(). Caller must free with rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_destroy().
requirements: rk must be a consumer configured with group.id, else NULL may be returned
Caller must destroy the returned object

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_new
functions.description: Create a new consumer group metadata object with only group_id set. Typically for tests.
requirements: group_id must be a valid non-NULL string
Caller must destroy returned object with rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_destroy()

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_new_with_genid
functions.signature: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_t *rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_new_with_genid(const char *group_id, int32_t generation_id, const char *member_id, const char *group_instance_id);
functions.description: Create a new consumer group metadata object with full fields (group id, generation/member epoch, member id, optional group instance id). Typically for tests.
requirements: group_id must be non-NULL
member_id may be NULL? (header does not forbid; docs indicate required) – if provided must be valid string
Caller must destroy returned object

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_group_id
functions.description: Return the group id from a consumer group metadata object. Pointer lifetime is tied to the metadata object.
requirements: group_metadata must be non-NULL and valid
Do not free returned pointer

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_group_instance_id
functions.description: Return the group instance id from a consumer group metadata object, or NULL.
requirements: group_metadata must be valid
Do not free returned pointer

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_member_id
functions.description: Return the member id from a consumer group metadata object. Pointer lifetime equals metadata object.
requirements: group_metadata must be valid
Do not free returned pointer

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_generation_id
functions.description: Return the generation id (classic protocol) or member epoch (consumer protocol) from the metadata.
requirements: group_metadata must be valid

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_destroy
functions.description: Destroy/free a consumer group metadata object previously created or returned by APIs.
requirements: It is permitted to pass NULL? (not stated; pass valid pointer)
Do not use object after destroying

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_write
functions.description: Serialize consumer group metadata to an opaque private binary format for in-process use (e.g., language bindings). Caller must free returned buffer with rd_kafka_mem_free().
requirements: cgmd must be valid
On success, *bufferp points to allocated memory and *sizep set; free with rd_kafka_mem_free(rk?, ptr). The docs: use rd_kafka_mem_free().
Returned error must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL

functions.name: rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_read
functions.description: Deserialize a previously serialized consumer group metadata buffer back into a metadata object. Caller must destroy the object.
requirements: buffer and size must reference a buffer produced by rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_write() in the same process/runtime
On success, *cgmdp is set and must be destroyed with rd_kafka_consumer_group_metadata_destroy()
Returned error must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL

functions.name: rd_kafka_produce
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_produce(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int msgflags, void *payload, size_t len, const void *key, size_t keylen, void *msg_opaque);
functions.description: Asynchronously produce a single message to a topic/partition. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure with errno set. Delivery reports are served by rd_kafka_poll()/rd_kafka_flush() if configured.
requirements: rkt must be created by rd_kafka_topic_new()
partition is RD_KAFKA_PARTITION_UA or 0..N
If RD_KAFKA_MSG_F_COPY not set, payload memory must remain valid until delivery callback; with RD_KAFKA_MSG_F_FREE librdkafka frees it on success
If returns -1 and RD_KAFKA_MSG_F_FREE was set, caller must still free payload
Key pointer may be NULL; keylen valid if key non-NULL
If msgflags includes RD_KAFKA_MSG_F_BLOCK and callbacks used, application MUST poll to drain delivery reports to avoid deadlock

functions.name: rd_kafka_producev
functions.description: Varargs producer API to produce a single message by specifying tagged parameters (RD_KAFKA_V_* tags), terminated by RD_KAFKA_V_END. Returns RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR_NO_ERROR on success.
requirements: Must terminate varargs with RD_KAFKA_V_END
Do not mix RD_KAFKA_V_HEADER and RD_KAFKA_V_HEADERS in the same call (returns RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR__CONFLICT)
Allowed tags include TOPIC, RKT, PARTITION, VALUE, KEY, OPAQUE, MSGFLAGS, TIMESTAMP, HEADER, HEADERS
If transactional.id is configured, producing is only allowed between begin_transaction() and commit/abort

functions.name: rd_kafka_produceva
functions.description: Vector-based variant of producev() using an array of tagged values (rd_kafka_vu_t). Returns NULL on success, or an error object on failure.
requirements: vus must contain a valid sequence of tags and values; cnt is the array length
Returned error object must be destroyed with rd_kafka_error_destroy() if non-NULL
Same semantics as rd_kafka_producev() regarding headers conflict and transactional constraints

functions.name: rd_kafka_produce_batch
functions.signature: int rd_kafka_produce_batch(rd_kafka_topic_t *rkt, int32_t partition, int msgflags, rd_kafka_message_t *rkmessages, int message_cnt);
functions.description: Produce multiple messages in one call. If partition==UA the configured partitioner is used. Returns the number of messages enqueued; per-message .err is set on each input element for failures.
requirements: rkt must be valid
rkmessages array must contain payload,len and optionally key,key_len,_private; .err will be set per message
If RD_KAFKA_MSG_F_PARTITION is set, use rkmessages[].partition rather than function partition arg
Headers are not supported via this API
Application must poll/flush to serve delivery reports

functions.name: rd_kafka_flush
functions.description: Block until all outstanding produce requests (and events) are completed or timeout_ms elapses. Calls rd_kafka_poll() unless RD_KAFKA_EVENT_DR is enabled, in which case it waits for internal message count to reach zero.
requirements: timeout_ms >= 0 (use -1? header allows int; semantics defined)
If RD_KAFKA_EVENT_DR is enabled, application must serve the event queue in another thread
Using flush ignores linger.ms to send queued messages ASAP

functions.name: rd_kafka_purge
functions.description: Purge messages currently handled by the producer. Flags select purging of internal queues (RD_KAFKA_PURGE_F_QUEUE), in-flight messages (RD_KAFKA_PURGE_F_INFLIGHT), and non-blocking behavior (RD_KAFKA_PURGE_F_NON_BLOCKING). Purged messages will yield delivery reports with PURGE_* errors.
requirements: rk must be a producer instance
Be aware purging in-flight messages voids future acknowledgements; retries may cause duplicates
Application must poll/flush to serve DR callbacks of purged messages
purge_flags must be a valid combination of RD_KAFKA_PURGE_F_*

functions.name: rd_kafka_metadata
functions.signature: rd_kafka_resp_err_t rd_kafka_metadata(rd_kafka_t *rk, int all_topics, rd_kafka_topic_t *only_rkt, const struct rd_kafka_metadata **metadatap, int timeout_ms);
functions.description: Request cluster metadata (brokers, topics, partitions). If all_topics!=0, request for all topics, else only locally known topics or only_rkt if provided. On success sets *metadatap; caller must destroy with rd_kafka_metadata_destroy().
requirements: timeout_ms >= 0
